title: Velop node showing solid red
fullDescription: A solid red LED on Velop indicates no internet connectivity. The gateway node can't reach WAN or a child node can't reach the gateway. Setup cannot complete while red LED is active.

causes.cause: Mesh node too far from primary

symptoms: Internet indicator off in Linksys app

fixSteps.title: Reseat WAN cable
fixSteps.instruction: Swap Ethernet between modem and Velop primary.

fixSteps.title: Relocate child node
fixSteps.instruction: Move within 1-2 rooms of primary to re-sync mesh.

faq.a: No – it almost always indicates WAN or mesh connectivity.

title: Velop child node offline in app
shortDescription: Child node can't be reached by the primary.
fullDescription: Offline nodes can result from power loss, distance, or firmware issue. The Linksys app shows them grayed out.

fixSteps.title: Remove & re-add
fixSteps.instruction: Linksys app > node > delete, then add node back.

whenToCallPro: Linksys support for replacement if repeated offline after reset.

faq.q: How many nodes can I add?
faq.a: Up to 6 in a single Velop mesh.

title: Velop firmware update not completing
shortDescription: Update stalls mid-install and node shows purple.
fullDescription: Firmware updates are automatic but can stall due to backhaul issues or Linksys Cloud outages. Nodes may flash purple or blue indefinitely.

fixSteps.title: Wait 30 minutes
fixSteps.instruction: Firmware may continue to install; don't unplug prematurely.

fixSteps.title: Factory reset last resort
fixSteps.instruction: Reset pinhole 10 seconds, then set up fresh.

whenToCallPro: Linksys support if reset doesn't clear the update.

title: Velop node lost backhaul
shortDescription: Child node dropped off the mesh backbone.
fullDescription: Tri-band Velop uses a dedicated 5 GHz backhaul; dual-band shares client traffic. Disconnections often happen when dedicated backhaul is blocked by walls.

fixSteps.title: Spot Finder
fixSteps.instruction: Linksys app > Wi-Fi > Spot Finder to test ideal placement.

fixSteps.title: Relocate
fixSteps.instruction: Line of sight to primary preferred.

faq.a: Yes on most Velop models via Ethernet between nodes.

title: Wi-Fi connects but no internet
shortDescription: Clients have Wi-Fi but no browsing.
fullDescription: Velop shows green but clients can't reach sites due to DNS, double-NAT, or ISP provisioning.

fixSteps.title: Bridge modem
fixSteps.instruction: Call ISP to set modem bridge mode.

title: Linksys app can't pair Velop
fullDescription: App uses BLE to commission the Velop. Missing permissions or distant phone causes failure.

causes.cause: Node not in setup LED state

fixSteps.title: Enable Bluetooth/Location
fixSteps.instruction: Turn on BT and grant app location permission.

fixSteps.title: Reset node
fixSteps.instruction: Hold reset 10 seconds until LED blinks red, release.

faq.q: Can I set up via web?
faq.a: Yes, browse http://velop.setup after wired connection.

title: Velop slower than subscribed plan
fullDescription: Velop throughput depends on model (AX4200 vs MX5300). Testing over Wi-Fi close to primary is a better baseline than far nodes.

fixSteps.title: 5 GHz client
fixSteps.instruction: Force test device to 5 GHz close to primary.

fixSteps.title: Contact ISP
fixSteps.instruction: If wired low too, ISP provisioning issue.

faq.a: Up to ~940 Mbps on gigabit WAN models.

title: Sites won't resolve on Velop network
fullDescription: DNS failures often caused by an unreachable custom DNS or Parental Controls block.

fixSteps.title: Disable parental controls
fixSteps.instruction: Temporarily disable to rule out filter.

whenToCallPro: ISP if automatic DNS also fails.

faq.a: No built-in DNS over HTTPS; rely on custom DNS.

title: Velop hot and rebooting
shortDescription: Thermal events drop clients and reboot nodes.
fullDescription: Velop passive cooling needs open airflow. Stacking and direct sun are common triggers.
